items.title: OpenAI gave ChatGPT a wallet
items.oneliner: OpenAI's new Wallet lets ChatGPT buy things with approval, pushing agents from demos into real transactional workflows.

items.title: Claude added spreadsheet-style analysis
items.oneliner: Claude Sheets turns quote comparison into a native table workflow, which is exactly how AI starts replacing lightweight analyst tasks.

items.title: Qwen's conversation state got mapped
items.oneliner: A Qwen3-1.7B probe mapped 900 Q and A examples across 100 topics, making conversation geometry less hand-wavy.

items.title: Public workers won AI job protections
items.oneliner: Oakland and New York are formalizing retraining over layoffs, which means AI labor rules are finally becoming contract language.

items.title: Bots are spoofing Kagi referrers
items.oneliner: Fake kagi.com referrals surged from Singapore, showing analytics pipelines are now easy targets for bot laundering.

items.title: DRAM price-fixing case moves forward
items.oneliner: A US judge let the DRAM conspiracy suit proceed, spotlighting how AI memory demand may be distorting the broader chip market.

items.title: US chip controls face internal pressure
items.oneliner: Commerce Secretary Lutnick reportedly pushed to weaken Southeast Asia chip rules, a reminder that AI export controls remain politically fragile.

items.title: Database branches now spin up instantly
items.oneliner: db-branch uses ZFS copy-on-write to clone MySQL and Postgres in seconds, which is catnip for CI and agent testing.

items.title: FreeBSD bhyve gained live migration
items.oneliner: FreeBSD 15.1 adds bhyve live migration over TCP, giving smaller infra teams a real maintenance and failover upgrade.

items.title: LangChain reportedly hit a $3B valuation
items.oneliner: LangChain reportedly raised $300 million at a $3 billion valuation, despite growing pressure on orchestration-layer differentiation.
